sentences.text: Marmornectes was an extinct genus of pliosaurid from the Middle Jurassic of Bedfordshire, United Kingdom.
This longirostrine pliosaurid possessed seven unique features and resembles Peloneustes philarchus.
Its name translates to "marble-swimmer," blending Latin and Greek roots.
The specific name candrewi honors Chris Andrew, who discovered and donated the sole specimen.
Hilary F. Ketchum and Roger B. J. Benson formally named the genus and its type species in 2011.
Cladistic analysis suggests this animal is basal to Peloneustes and other pliosaurids.
It lived during the early Callovian stage, approximately 164.7 to 163.5 million years ago.
